extracted.intended_audience: researchers (Principal Investigators) preparing ERC Synergy Grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/evaluation rules for preparing and submitting an ERC Synergy Grant proposal (collaborative proposal by 2–4 PIs under Horizon Europe). Covers who can apply, host institution requirements, budget, ethics review, evaluation steps and submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants — number and role of PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: A group of two to maximum four Principal Investigators (PIs) working together and bringing different skills and resources to tackle ambitious research problems. One will be designated as the corresponding PI (cPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No specific eligibility criteria regarding the academic training are foreseen. Portability applies to each PI. PIs must present a competitive track record as appropriate to their career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole evaluation criterion — scientific excellence with synergetic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated on the sole criterion of scientific excellence which takes on the additional meaning of outstanding intrinsic synergetic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excellence applies to both the research project and the Principal Investigators, taking into account the synergetic aspects of the proposed research and the PIs. Evaluators are international peer reviewers who assess proposals solely on excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research cannot be carried out by a single PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must demonstrate that the proposed research cannot be carried out by a single PI working alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synergy Grants target research problems so ambitious they require complementary skills/resources from multiple PIs; the proposal must justify the added value of the synergy between PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution (HI) and location requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted by all PIs in a public or private research organisation (Host Institution, HI) established in one of the EU Member States or associated countries. One PI per Synergy Grant group at any one time can be hosted or engaged by an institution outside of the EU or associated countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It could be the HI where the applicant already works, or any other eligible HI. Where different PIs are hosted by more than one HI, each HI shall offer their support to the PI(s) hosted by them for the duration of the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution commitments and support letters
rubrics_metrics.description: At submission stage, all Host Institutions must provide the host support letter for their Principal Investigator(s). The ERC Synergy Grant is awarded to the cHI that engages and hosts the cPI and to any other HI that engages and hosts other PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions must engage the PIs for at least the duration of the grant and must offer appropriate conditions for PIs to independently direct the proposed research and manage the project's funding. If a PI is not at the HI at submission, a supplementary agreement and commitment from the HI are necessary should the proposal be successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and participating researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC Synergy grants support projects carried out by a group of two to four individual researchers who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members. It is also possible to have one or more team members located in a third country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacancies for team members can be published on the Euraxess-Jobs portal. The written consent of any researcher mentioned in the proposal as participating in the project is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and project duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Synergy Grants can be up to a maximum of €10 million for a period of 6 years (pro rata for projects of shorter duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An additional €4 million can be requested in total to cover eligible 'start-up' costs for researchers moving from a third country to the EU or an associated country and/or the purchase of major equipment and/or access to large facilities and/or other major experimental and field work costs. An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents. ERC grant applications can only be submitted in response to a Call for Proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls are published on the ERC page, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and in the Official Journal. Submit by the specified closing date; you can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by submitting a new version which overwrites the old one. You will get an acknowledgement of receipt by e-mail for each submission. Submit as early as possible to avoid unforeseen difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process structure — three steps including interview
rubrics_metrics.description: A single submission of the full proposal is followed by a three-step evaluation, including interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: Part I of the scientific proposal and the PIs’ CV and Track Record will be assessed by the evaluation panel (and not the full scientific proposal). Step 2: The complete version of the Research proposal will be assessed (CVs and Track record, Parts I and II of the Scientific Proposal, Resources and Time commitment and Budget table annex). Step 3: Principal Investigators will be invited for an interview to present their project to a panel in Brussels; the most competitive retained proposals are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Synergy evaluations will be unique, fit for complex projects and without predefined panels. Panel Members are selected by the ERC Scientific Council on the basis of their scientific reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1 panel is formed from approximately 90 panel members and chairs. Five to seven panels in step 2 will be formed dynamically after step 1 filtering to ensure best expertise. Step 3 interview panels may be reconfigured. Evaluation relies on panel members acting as 'generalists' plus input from external experts (remote evaluators) who bring specialised expertise but do not participate in panel meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring, quality threshold and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who pass the quality threshold at step 3 - scored 'A' - are ranked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been exhausted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on contacting reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are requested not to contact reviewers under any circumstances as they risk having their proposal rejected from the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct contact with reviewers is explicitly forbidden and may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review requirement and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: If your proposal is selected for funding it will undergo an ethics review. This is a legal requirement under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme - Regulation 2021/695: Eligible actions and ethical principles (Article 18) and Ethics (Article 19). The basis for this ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table – EIT – and the Ethics Self-Assessment – ESA) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-detailed ESA is crucial to facilitate the process as it clarifies what issues are linked to the proposed research activities and how these will be dealt with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review stages and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethics review comprises 3 stages: Ethics pre-screening (performed internally by ERCEA staff), Ethics screening (panels of independent ethics reviewers identify proposals with potentially Serious and/or Complex ethics issues) and Ethics assessment (panels of independent ethics reviewers discuss Serious and/or Complex issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearance of proposals with non-Serious and/or Complex ethics issues can include observations and references to documents to be kept on file and provided to ERCEA upon request only. After screening, applicants might be contacted to provide additional information (typically one week after screening) and are given 3 weeks to reply. In case of Serious/Complex issues, ethics deliverables might be formulated and followed-up during implementation. Research involving the use of hESCs will need all steps of ethics review plus a specific EC approval following a consultation to the HE programme committee (comitology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance, support and required familiarisation with submission systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should read the call related documents (ERC Work Programme and Information to Applicants), familiarise themselves with the EU submission service (online system through which proposals must be submitted) and the Online Manual, and contact the Host Institution and National Contact Point (NCP) for support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elaborate the research idea with other PIs and consider synergetic aspects; work tightly with other PIs and allow time for reviews of draft proposals. NCPs, peers and other scientists can provide helpful support. Use the ERC dashboard and ERIS for data on funded projects and evaluated proposals.
